headline: UK cyber chief warns of AI-powered attacks on infrastructure; FBI ties Binance heist to North Korea; GitLab and Ivanti attacks continue

bullets.text: New: the UK's NCSC says its cyber chief warns the UK faces AI-powered attacks on critical infrastructure within two years. The Record reports a warning of an 'unprecedented rise' in cyberattacks in the coming months.

New: DataBreaches.net reports the hackers who hit UNM hospital apologized, offered patients $2,500 and revealed more in a new statement. It also reports a breach at HYBE in South Korea exposing employee medical records and financial details.

Binance, 7 outlets: The Register reports the FBI pins the $6.3B heist on North Korean hackers; SecurityWeek says the FBI flagged over 600 addresses. Separately, The Record reports Brazil's largest crypto exchange confirmed a cyberattack as millions flowed out.

BleepingComputer reports over 1,000 GitLab servers are vulnerable to ongoing RCE attacks. CISA KEV lists GitLab CE/EE flaw CVE-2026-97229, whose federal due date passed on 2026-11-01. Alpine Linux rebuilt its GitLab after an attempted RCE attack.

Connect Secure, 5 outlets: Ivanti patched two more zero-days chained in attacks, CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527. CISA KEV lists CVE-2026-104935 in the same product, with federal due dates of 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-13.

Claude, 3 outlets: SecurityWeek reports a malicious Claude Code extension served in a Cursor supply chain attack. Separately, The Hacker News reports the VOLTA infostealer uses Claude, Gemini and Kimi AI to rank victims by financial value.

actions: Patch GitLab CE/EE (CVE-2026-97229) and Cisco ASA/FTD (CVE-2026-76418) now; both KEV due dates have passed. Check GitLab servers for signs of RCE.
Apply Ivanti's latest Connect Secure patches, covering CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527, and check appliances for compromise.
Find any Langflow, LXD and MicroCloud servers, check vendor advisories for the critical flaws, and patch. Restrict access to any you cannot patch yet.
If developers use the Claude Code extension in Cursor, check it against the vendor advisory and look for unexpected SSH keys or services.
Review infostealer detections, and rotate credentials and tokens on any host found infected.
If you handle crypto transactions, screen against the addresses the FBI flagged for the Binance heist, and warn staff about Binance-themed scams.
